title: Conversations — The Third Chair
subtitle: Two siblings clearing an estate must decide who keeps an empty chair.
subheading: Episode II: Two siblings clearing an estate must decide who keeps an empty chair.
author: Terminal Musing

content.text: [Setting: The dining room of a century-old stone farmhouse. The floor is covered in half-taped cardboard boxes and rolls of bubble wrap. Dust motes dance in the late-afternoon sunbeam.]
[Characters: TARIQ, forty, practical, holding an inventory clipboard. AMIRA, thirty-seven, sitting cross-legged on the floor, holding a porcelain teacup with a hairline fracture.]
TARIQ: Everything has a recipient except the elm wood chairs. The dealer from town offered four hundred for the set.
TARIQ: There are four chairs, Amira. A set of three is worthless to a dealer.
AMIRA: The third one has Father's initials carved under the left rung. Look at it.
TARIQ: (Sighs, lowering the clipboard) I know what is carved under the rung. I was nine when he did it. He used the penknife I dropped in the cistern.
AMIRA: Then how can you price it at one hundred dollars?
TARIQ: Because memory doesn't pay for the roof leak in the barn. We are burying a life, Amira, not museum-curating a tragedy.
AMIRA: When Mother fell ill, you were in Chicago. You didn't sit in that chair for nine months while her breath got shorter every evening. That chair kept the vigil, Tariq. You didn't.
TARIQ: (Freezes. His jaw tightens. He walks over to the third chair, placing both hands on the curved elm top rail.) Do you think being absent means being spared?
AMIRA: (Her voice drops to a whisper) I didn't say that.
TARIQ: (Quietly) Take the chair, Amira. Take all four. I'll pay the dealer his penalty.
